oneliner.t: Four-term Democratic U.S. representative for New Hampshire's 1st District and co-owner of Manchester's Puritan Backroom restaurant, who won the Sept. 8, 2026 Democratic primary and faces Republican John E. Sununu for the open Senate seat Jeanne Shaheen is leaving.

born.t: June 4, 1980, Manchester, New Hampshire (Wikipedia; Voteview lists birth year 1980)

upbringing.t: Christopher Charles Pappas was born in Manchester to Dawn and Arthur Pappas. His great-grandfather, a Greek immigrant, co-founded a Manchester ice cream shop in 1917 that became the Puritan Backroom restaurant, which the family still owns. He graduated from Manchester Central High School in 1998 and from Harvard College (B.A., government) in 2002, and first volunteered in politics for Jeanne Shaheen's 1996 governor's campaign. He was elected to the New Hampshire House the year he graduated. He is Greek Orthodox and married Vann Bentley in February 2023. He is the first openly gay man to represent New Hampshire in Congress.

career.role: County Treasurer (lost 2010 bid for a third term)
Co-owner/manager of family restaurant (minority owner; 2025 LLC income $140,889)
career.org: Puritan Backroom (Puritan Confectionery Co.) and Pilgrim Realty, Manchester

platform.t: 'Tax Cuts and Lower Costs Blueprint': cut energy taxes, protect LIHEAP heating aid, defend clean-energy tax credits, suspend the federal gas tax (with Sen. Mark Kelly), oppose tariffs on groceries and essentials.
Says he helped cap insulin costs and let Medicare negotiate drug prices; calls for reversing health-care cuts affecting New Hampshire.

Takes no corporate PAC money (campaign claim), lead House sponsor of the DISCLOSE Act, supports overturning Citizens United and a ban on congressional stock trading, and a bill to codify the congressional ethics office.
Supports a federal law restoring abortion rights after Dobbs.
Opposes abolishing ICE; wants oversight and reforms, enforcement focused on serious criminal offenders, and due process. Voted for the Laken Riley Act in January 2025.

Backs a two-state solution and humanitarian aid to Gaza. In April 2026 said the Iran war changed his view and he would vote to limit certain arms sales to Israel; called Netanyahu's recent actions 'indefensible and unsupportable.'
Calls the 2026 Iran war a 'war of choice', supports war-powers resolutions to limit it, and calls for efforts to end it.
Leading an effort to build New Hampshire's first full-service VA hospital (campaign testimonial).
More investment in affordable housing and lower energy costs.

promises.t: Keep refusing corporate PAC money and pass the DISCLOSE Act.
Suspend the federal gas tax and cut energy taxes.
Build the first VA hospital in New Hampshire.
Ban stock trading by members of Congress.
Vote to limit certain arms sales to Israel (April 2026 statement).

note.t: 2025 annual report (filed Aug. 13, 2026 under an extension): biggest asset is his minority stake in the family restaurant company Puritan Confectionery Co. ($1M–$5M, $140,889 LLC income) plus minority interests in two Manchester properties through Pilgrim Realty. A Wells Fargo IRA holds about 30 diversified mutual funds; the 24 reported 2025 transactions were all mutual-fund buys/sells inside that IRA (Jan. 13 and Aug. 18, 2025), not individual stocks, so no committee overlap. Spouse holds Uber stock and RSUs ($200K–$500K total) from his Uber employment, and a Fidelity 401(k). Liabilities: home mortgage, a second-home mortgage ($500K–$1M, joint), a HELOC, the spouse's student loan, a 2005 stock-purchase loan from Arthur Pappas and a 2019 member stock-purchase loan from Puritan Confectionery ($250K–$500K). Schedule G lists $7,609.61 in NH Lottery winnings. No foreign assets or income; no outside positions besides the two family LLCs. Net-worth range = disclosed assets minus non-mortgage liabilities (home and second home not listed as assets, so their mortgages and the HELOC are excluded); including all liabilities the range is about -$392K to $6.08M.

checks.claims: Mechanical v2.1 sample: (a) every checkable claim on chrispappas.org/about-chris (8 rated; the page appears outdated, e.g. 'third term'); (b) the campaign has two 'priority' pages; the first 10 statements of the Tax Cuts and Lower Costs Blueprint were reviewed — #1–3, #6, #7, #9, #10 are positions or third-party testimonials too vague to check, #4, #5, #8 are rated, plus #11–12 because so few items were checkable; from the Anti-Corruption Agenda #2, #3, #4, #6 rated; (c) ad spend unknown, so the Aug. 11, 2026 TV and digital ads (campaign release) were used — their claims (no corporate PAC money, DISCLOSE Act, Sununu $35M) are rated.

research_notes: ACCESS: fec.gov, congress.gov, GovTrack, Track AIPAC, CourtListener, the campaign homepage and most news links were not fetchable from this tool (only pages that appeared in the 12 permitted web searches, plus Wikipedia, could be opened), so money relies on the on-disk FEC records file (data as of 2026-10-13, coverage through 2026-08-19). MONEY: the records file has only his 2026 Senate cycle; his House cycles (H8NH01210, 2018–2024) were not available and need adding from fec.gov. pac_biz = labor $159,500 + trade $50,000 + membership $44,812 + corporate $4,500; pac_ideo = ideological $85,050 + leadership PACs $417,500 + hybrid/super PAC direct $70,080; 'other' = candidate committees $26,446. These add to $865,388 vs. FEC 'PACs and committees' $1,104,873; the gap (likely joint-fundraising transfers) is not broken out. Itemized vs. unitemized individual split not available. instate_pct 0.194 = 1 minus the 80.6% out-of-state share OpenSecrets reported for his latest report (via NH Bulletin), not the whole cycle. NH Bulletin reported $14.6M raised through Aug. 19 vs. $15.38M in FEC totals; FEC figure used. The pre-general report (due Oct. 22) is not yet reflected. Outside-spending totals are FEC Schedule E sums through about Oct. 1, 2026; super PAC donor lists were not checked. ISRAEL: AIPAC career figure is a news lower bound; AIPAC PAC earmark totals and Track AIPAC were not checked directly. The July 2026 'present' vote's roll-call number and amendment sponsor need a human check on clerk.house.gov. NOT CHECKED: key-vote roll calls (handled by the separate key-vote pass), statements on the 2020/2024 results, courts, House Ethics/OCC, debates (no debate was reported in any source opened; access counts omitted), town halls. NRSC described his spouse as an 'Amazon lobbyist' (Union Leader); his 2025 disclosure lists spouse salary from Uber. A spouse's job is not the candidate's record and was not researched further.
